public_body: Gloucester Community Arts Charter School Board Of Trustees
overall: After the charter surrender and school closure, the AG ordered the Board to release its March 2012 executive session minutes (subject to privilege and exemptions), closed the remaining complaints as withdrawn, and referred non-minutes records requests to the Public Records Division.

allegations.summary: Complainant sought release of the Board's March 24 and March 31, 2012 executive session minutes; the Board did not respond to the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Despite the closure decision, the Board has a continuing obligation as it winds down its affairs to comply with the Open Meeting Law and make meeting minutes available to the public.

allegations.summary: Four other complaints filed in 2011 and 2012 by the same complainant were closed after he offered to withdraw them.
allegations.key_passage: Consistent with the agreement with Mr. Grow, we now consider his complaints closed.

allegations.summary: Complainant's request for release of documents other than minutes, such as written communications between Board members, falls outside the AG's Open Meeting Law review.
allegations.key_passage: If Mr. Grow wishes to appeal the denial of requests for documents other than meeting minutes, such as written communications between Board members, he may do so by contacting the Supervisor of Public Records within the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Public Records Division.

remedy: Release the executive session minutes of the March 24, 2012 and March 31, 2012 meetings, unless the attorney-client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies to withhold all or part of them.
remedy_passage: We therefore order the Board to release the executive session minutes of its March 24, 2012 and March 31, 2012 meetings, unless the attorney-client privilege or one or more of the exemptions to the Public Records Law applies to withhold the minutes, or any portion thereof, from disclosure.
